docs_intro_what_is_body: ECOMAP (Constrained Optimization of Metabolic Models & Analysis Pipeline) is a computational framework for constructing, calibrating and applying enzyme-constrained genome-scale metabolic models (ecGEMs). It turns a genome-scale metabolic model (GEM) into a calibrated, design-ready ecGEM through four cooperating modules: Reconstruction, Calibration, Analysis, and Design.
docs_intro_ecmodel_body: An ecGEM extends a GEM with enzyme-capacity constraints. Every reaction is paired with a turnover number (kcat) and a molecular weight; the solver then bounds flux by the available enzyme budget. This produces predictions of protein allocation, growth-yield ceilings, and resource bottlenecks that a plain stoichiometric model cannot.
docs_intro_why_body: Pure GEMs treat enzymes as infinite catalysts. Real cells compete for ribosomes, chaperones, and proteostasis capacity. Adding the enzyme budget brings simulations closer to measured physiology -- growth rates, overflow metabolism, and stress responses -- and makes the model useful for engineering decisions.
docs_framework_body: The pipeline runs left to right. Each stage consumes the artifact of the previous one and writes a new artifact for the next.
docs_modules_body: The four modules form a chain. You usually run them in order, but each can also be used standalone if you already have the right input.
tutorial_gs_install_body: ECOMAP runs as a MATLAB package. Clone the repository and add its paths once per session by calling setup at the MATLAB prompt. The Python backend is bootstrapped automatically on first start.
tutorial_gs_env_body: MATLAB R2019b or later with the JVM enabled. Python 3.9-3.12 (auto-detected; override via scripts/web/server/.ecomap-python). Roughly 2 GB of free disk for the venv and model uploads.
tutorial_gs_inputs_body: You will need a GEM in one of: .mat, .xml (SBML), .json, or .yml. For enzyme-constrained workflows also provide a kcat database (BRENDA / SABIO-RK export) and optional proteomics measurements.
tutorial_gs_workflow_body: Launch the web UI with ecomapWeb('start'), open the browser at http://127.0.0.1:8000, and pick the module that matches your immediate goal. Most users start with Reconstruction, then move on to Calibration, Analysis, and finally Design.
tutorial_workflow_body: A canonical ECOMAP run walks five steps. Skip the ones you do not need; everything else is a no-op when its prerequisites are missing.
tutorial_wf_step1_body: Load a curated genome-scale model from ecYeast, eciML1515, eciCW773, or ecHuman, or import your own. Validate reaction and metabolite IDs are non-empty and the biomass reaction is set.
tutorial_wf_step2_body: Run Reconstruction. The wizard merges in enzyme information, assigns kcat values from your database, and writes an enzyme-constrained genome-scale model next to your input.
tutorial_wf_step3_body: Run Calibration. Growth-rate targets and optional proteomics steer the kcat and sigma tuning.
tutorial_wf_step4_body: Run Analysis to inspect FVA ranges, enzyme-cost hotspots, and parameter sensitivities.
tutorial_wf_step5_body: Run Design to propose knockout / overexpression interventions. The output is a ranked candidate list that you can export to CSV.
tutorial_recon_intro: Reconstruction turns a GEM into an ecGEM. Five steps, each with a clear input and output.
tutorial_recon_step1_body: Open the Reconstruction workspace. Pick your GEM file in loadModel. The wizard checks IDs, biomass reaction, and metabolite formulas. Bad inputs fail fast with a clear error code.
tutorial_recon_step2_body: Upload a kcat database (BRENDA or SABIO-RK TSV). ECOMAP indexes by EC number and matches against your model's reactions. Unmatched reactions are logged for manual review.
tutorial_recon_step3_body: For each matched reaction ECOMAP picks a kcat value, falling back to the median of the source database when no exact match exists. You can override any individual value in the table view.
tutorial_recon_step4_body: Click Generate ecGEM. The wizard writes the enzyme-constrained model alongside your input, plus a JSON sidecar describing every assumption made.
tutorial_recon_step5_body: Inspect the auto-generated QC report: reaction coverage, kcat distribution, growth-rate prediction vs. measured, and a list of any reactions that still need manual curation.
tutorial_calib_intro: Calibration tunes kcat values and sigma factors so the ecGEM predicts measured physiology. Five steps; each is independent of the next.
tutorial_calib_step1_body: Upload a TSV with two columns: condition (e.g. carbon source, oxygen level) and growth_rate (1/h). At least three conditions spanning a 5x range are recommended.
tutorial_calib_step2_body: ECOMAP solves the ecGEM at each condition and minimizes the residual to your measurements. A regularization term keeps the kcats close to the database priors.
tutorial_calib_step3_body: Optional: upload 13C-fluxomics data. ECOMAP fits the kcat pool to match measured uptake / secretion rates alongside the growth targets.
tutorial_calib_step4_body: Switch to the Bayesian fit mode for uncertainty quantification. Output includes 95% credible intervals for every fitted kcat.
tutorial_calib_step5_body: The validation tab compares model predictions against held-out conditions. R-squared greater than 0.8 is a typical good fit; below 0.5 suggests the input GEM is missing key reactions.
tutorial_analysis_intro: Analysis answers questions about your calibrated ecGEM. Five common analyses, ordered by complexity.
tutorial_analysis_step1_body: Run a single FBA to confirm growth-rate parity with measurements. This is the smoke test before doing anything more elaborate.
tutorial_analysis_step2_body: FVA returns the feasible range for every reaction. Reactions with a narrow range are bottlenecks; reactions with a wide range are candidates for intervention.
tutorial_analysis_step3_body: Plot the top 20 reactions by enzyme cost. These are the reactions where a small kcat change has the largest flux impact.
tutorial_analysis_step4_body: Perturb each kcat by plus/minus 10% and report the resulting change in target flux. Reactions with high elasticity are your leverage points.
tutorial_analysis_step5_body: Combine the three views above into a short report. The standard layout is: bottlenecks (FVA) to leverage points (sensitivity) to protein cost (enzyme usage).
tutorial_design_intro: Design proposes genetic interventions that improve a target flux. Five steps from objective to ranked candidate list.
tutorial_design_step1_body: Pick the target reaction (e.g. a product biosynthesis reaction) and a minimum acceptable flux improvement (e.g. 50%). The wizard stores this in the design session.
tutorial_design_step2_body: ECOMAP enumerates single and double knockouts, plus overexpression candidates (top 20 by enzyme cost). Larger combinations require the optKnock / OptForce add-on.
tutorial_design_step3_body: Choose between FSEOF (fast, linear) and OptKnock / OptForce (slower, more thorough). FSEOF is the default for fewer than 200 candidates.
tutorial_design_step4_body: Run the algorithm. Output is a ranked table: intervention, predicted target flux, growth-rate impact, number of genes.
tutorial_design_step5_body: Export the top 5 candidates as CSV. The export includes the gene IDs in standard nomenclature so it drops directly into your strain-design workflow.
modules_intro: Four cooperating modules that turn a GEM into a calibrated, design-ready ecGEM. Create or open a project before running them.
